description: Understand why do journalists get killed and how to perform proactive risk assessment on your Mac to stay safe in the field.
intro: Journalists face high levels of physical and digital danger, often leading to the question of why do journalists get killed while reporting on the ground. The answer lies in the intersection of unstable environments, lack of institutional support, and insufficient risk assessment protocols that fail to account for escalating threats.
tldr: Risk assessment is the primary defense against physical and digital threats in journalism.
Cultural pressure in newsrooms often prevents reporters from conducting thorough safety checks.
You can use built-in macOS tools like FileVault to secure your data immediately.
Proactive planning with editors and security experts reduces the likelihood of trauma and injury.
Lazur helps you organize safety checklists and research security protocols using voice commands.

blocks.text: The reality of danger in modern reporting

When you ask why do journalists get killed, you must look at the lack of preparation. Many reporters enter hostile zones without a formal risk assessment. This process identifies potential physical, digital, and psychological threats. Without it, you are reacting to danger instead of avoiding it.
Why risk assessments are often ignored

Systemic pressures in newsrooms prioritize speed over safety. Editors often push for immediate output, leaving little time for security planning. There is also a culture of toughness. Admitting you need a safety plan is sometimes viewed as a sign of weakness.

items: Lack of standardized managerial strategies for reporter protection.
Freelance reporters often lack access to organizational security infrastructure.
Fear of losing assignments prevents reporters from requesting safety resources.
The assumption that safety is a personal responsibility rather than a newsroom duty.

blocks.text: Digital security fixes for your Mac
You can improve your digital safety today without spending money. Start with the tools already on your Mac. Encryption is the first step to protecting your sources and your research.

items: Enable FileVault: Open System Settings > Privacy and Security > FileVault to encrypt your drive.
Use strong passwords: Use a dedicated password manager to ensure every account has a unique, complex key.
Remove metadata: Use tools like MetaCleaner to strip location data from photos before you upload them.
Use encrypted messaging: Stick to Signal for all communications with sources.

blocks.text: How to structure your risk assessment
A good risk assessment is a living document. It should cover the location, the nature of the story, and the political climate. Use a scale of 1 to 5 to rate the likelihood and impact of each threat.

rows: Map out extraction points and local hospitals
Check device encryption and VPN status

faq.question: Why do journalists get killed in conflict zones?
faq.answer: Journalists are often targeted for their work, caught in crossfire, or kidnapped. Lack of proper risk assessment and protective gear significantly increases these risks.

faq.question: Can I perform a risk assessment by myself?
faq.answer: Yes, but it is better to do it with your editor. If you are a freelancer, use templates from organizations like the European Federation of Journalists.

faq.question: Is my Mac secure enough for sensitive reporting?
faq.answer: Your Mac is secure if you use FileVault and keep your software updated. Always use encrypted messaging apps and avoid public Wi-Fi without a VPN.

costs.title: Physical harm
costs.text: The ultimate cost is the loss of life or serious injury when safety protocols are absent.

costs.title: Trauma and burnout
costs.text: Constant exposure to danger without a support plan leads to long-term psychological impact and career-ending burnout.

costs.title: Data compromise
costs.text: Insecure devices lead to the exposure of sensitive source information and personal identity.

causes.title: Institutional neglect
causes.text: Many news organizations fail to provide formal safety training or risk assessment resources to staff.

causes.title: Cultural stigma
causes.text: The culture of journalism often discourages reporters from speaking up about safety concerns.

causes.title: Lack of time
causes.text: The pressure to meet deadlines often results in skipping essential safety checks.

fixes.title: Use standard assessment tools
fixes.text: Adopt the EFJ risk assessment platform to score and mitigate threats systematically.

fixes.title: Encrypt your Mac
fixes.text: Always enable FileVault in System Settings to protect your local data from unauthorized access.

fixes.title: Collaborate on safety
fixes.text: Make risk assessment a shared task with your editor rather than a solitary chore.
